questions.topic: Page 5: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 5-6 Focus)
questions.questionText: A point P(a, b) is plotted on a Cartesian plane such that its vertical distance from the origin is zero. Which of the following must be true regarding the coordinates of P?

options.optionText: The value of 'a' must be equal to 'b'.

questions.explanationAnswer: The vertical distance from the origin in a Cartesian plane is represented by the y-coordinate. If this distance is zero, the point must lie on the x-axis, meaning its y-coordinate (b) is 0.
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify the coordinate property corresponding to a zero vertical distance from the origin.

questions.topic: Page 5: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 5-6 Focus)
questions.questionText: A point Q has coordinates (-5, 8). In which quadrant of the Cartesian plane does this point lie?
questions.explanationAnswer: In the Cartesian coordinate system, Quadrant II is defined by a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate (-, +). Since -5 is negative and 8 is positive, the point lies in Quadrant II.
questions.explanationQuestion: Analyze the signs of the given coordinates (-5, 8) to determine their quadrant location.
